authority.rules: GURPS Lite, June 2003 (Third Edition-era introductory rules)

artifact_note.target: A G6-targeted Scenario 01 with Phase E bounded combat: one Rook broadsword attack, one bandit-scout Dodge reaction, one ST10 broadsword cutting damage path, injury/HP mutation, stun threshold, and deferred consciousness-check state.
artifact_note.assumptions: Scenario fiction, character values, encounter composition, and tutorial pacing are DIRPS prototype assumptions. GURPS mechanics remain sourced from GURPS Lite and must not be silently invented.
acceptance: A fresh runtime can load one DODGE 0.2.1 document plus the DIRPS proto sidecar and this scenario.
Play exercises an ordinary success roll, a social or reaction-oriented interaction, an environmental challenge, and one manageable combat exchange.
Every random result is preserved in replay evidence.
Every mechanical resolution can identify the rule/procedure used and its source locator.
Unsupported or uncertain rules fail visibly rather than being guessed.
artifact_note.acceptance_note: Phase E proves the attack -> active defense -> damage -> injury -> state-change sequence without implementing full GURPS combat. Phase F owns HT recovery/consciousness rolls after combat.

tutorial.title: The Missing Courier
tutorial.premise: A courier failed to return along an isolated road. The player follows the route, investigates what happened, deals with one grounded obstacle, and returns with an answer.
tutorial.design_goal: Teach core RPG resolution progressively while generating deterministic replay evidence for DIRPS/DODGE development.

encounters.purpose: Exercise an ordinary success roll with a situational modifier.

success.information_text: Rook identifies a clear trail leading away from the road.

failure.information_text: Rook cannot establish a reliable trail from the disturbed roadside signs.

encounters.purpose: Exercise a social/reaction-oriented resolution without requiring a large NPC subsystem.

actions.label: Reassure the frightened witness and ask what they saw

reaction_modifiers.reason: Scenario 01 treats this bounded reassuring approach as a good approach worth the minimum +1 behavior bonus described by GURPS Lite.

disastrous.information_text: The frightened witness recoils and refuses to give a usable account.

very-bad.information_text: The witness distrusts Rook and refuses to give a useful direction.

bad.information_text: The witness gives no reliable detail that advances the search.

poor.information_text: The witness remains too wary to offer a useful lead.

neutral.information_text: The witness confirms the courier left the road but cannot give a reliable direction.

good.information_text: The witness gives a useful direction for continuing the search toward the washed-out path.

very-good.information_text: The witness gives a clear, cooperative account pointing the search toward the washed-out path.

excellent.information_text: The witness eagerly provides the clearest available account and points Rook toward the washed-out path.

encounters.purpose: Exercise an attribute or skill test with clear consequences.

success.consequence_text: Rook crosses the washed-out section and can continue beyond the obstacle.

failure.consequence_text: Rook cannot cross safely and must take a detour before continuing.

encounters.purpose: Exercise attack, active defense, damage, injury, and state change in a bounded encounter.

actions.label: Attack the bandit scout with Rook's broadsword

canonical_here: which mechanics the tutorial intends to exercise
